title: Subsets II
statement: `nums` may contain duplicates. Return every unique subset, sorted internally and as a list.
hints: Sort so equal values are adjacent.
At each level, skip a value that equals the previous value when the previous value was not chosen.
That skip is what prevents emitting the same subset from two identical numbers.

approaches.name: Set of tuples
approaches.explanation: Generate the full power set and uniquify.

approaches.name: Sorted backtracking with a skip
approaches.explanation: Never start a branch on a duplicate that the previous sibling skipped.

editorial: Sort, then do the combination-style recursion that chooses a start index. Inside the loop, if i > start and nums[i] == nums[i - 1], continue. The first copy of a value is allowed to open the branch. Later copies are used only deeper, after that first copy was taken.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def subsets_with_dup(nums: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]:
    nums = sorted(nums)
    out: list[list[int]] = []
    path: list[int] = []

    def dfs(start: int) -> None:
        out.append(path[:])
        for i in range(start, len(nums)):
            if i > start and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]:
                continue
            path.append(nums[i])
            dfs(i + 1)
            path.pop()

    dfs(0)
    out.sort()
    return out
